title: Seagate Stock and Western Digital Tumble as Investors Worry AI Shortage Will Ease
source_used: Yahoo Finance (Proactive, 2 Oct 2026); a second Yahoo Finance piece (2 Oct, Gian Estrada, partly opinion) used only for cross-checking
key_facts: Seagate (STX) and Western Digital (WDC) shares fell on Friday 2 Oct 2026 after a report on Toshiba's planned production expansion.
Intraday: Seagate down about 13% to $825.47 and Western Digital down about 12% to $405.23 (the other Yahoo piece: Seagate about 12%, Western Digital about 10%).
Nikkei reported that Toshiba plans to invest about 60 billion yen (about $400 million) to double its hard disk drive production capacity by financial year 2027, centred on its Philippines factory.
Toshiba holds just over 10% of the hard drive market by capacity and has a medium-term target of 30%; the market is dominated by three firms (Seagate, Western Digital, Toshiba).
Seagate was up roughly 240% and Western Digital about 170% this year before the fall, which left both open to profit-taking.
Yahoo/Proactive says the expansion could pressure Seagate's and Western Digital's market share and pricing (a possibility, not a result).
quote_evidence: Seagate Technology Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:STX) and Western Digital Corp (NASDAQ:WDC) fell Friday after a report on Toshiba's planned production expansion raised concerns about tougher competition for AI data-center storage.
Nikkei reported that Toshiba plans to invest about ¥60 billion ($400 million) to double its hard disk drive production capacity by financial year 2027.
According to Nikkei, Toshiba currently holds just over 10% of that market based on capacity and has set a medium-term target of reaching 30%.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors fear a third hard drive maker adding capacity could weaken the pricing power Seagate and Western Digital gained from AI data-center demand.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (Nikkei report on Toshiba's plan appeared 2 Oct Tokyo time; shares fell the same day)
notes: Follow-up of 1002:C08-05 (Nikkei Asia: 'Toshiba to double hard disk drive supply to fill AI chip memory gap'). New today: the share-price reaction.
